newsitem.title: USA: KImbery-Clark sees earnings problems in Q2.
newsitem.headline: KImbery-Clark sees earnings problems in Q2.

text.p: Kimberly-Clark Corp said Thursday that although the company reported record earnings from operations in the first quarter, it expects second quarter results to be adversely impacted by softness in its away-from-home busines and by economic conditions in Mexico.
But the company added that it expected sales and earnings to improve in the third and fourth quarters.
The company also said that the sale of its Coosa Pines, Ala., newspsrint and pulp operation will have a negative impact on 1997 earnings of about $0.03 per share.

The company said that 1997 will be the final phase of its full transition from a diversified paper company to a global consumer products company, and that it has set an aggressive target of seeing its earnings per share from operations double from $1.93 in 1995 to at least $3.86 in the year 2000, as well as generate total return to our shareholders consistently in excess of the S&P 500.
The company said its strategies for product innovation, global expansion of its core businesses and divestiture of noncore operations will allow it to achieve those goals.
